description: Whether a failure in front of a real visitor reaches anybody. A site with no reporting is not a site with no errors; it is a site where the errors are only ever seen by the person who left.

gates.title: The Reporting Snippet Is In The Page
gates.rule: The error reporting snippet is present in the served HTML, not only in the repository. A snippet added to a template that the build does not use reports nothing and reads as done.
gates.fix: Add it to the document the build actually serves, then confirm it in the deployed page.

gates.title: The Collector Knows This Site
gates.rule: The site has an entry in the collector on the Pi, so a report arriving from it is attributed rather than dropped.
gates.fix: Run /onboard-error-reporting, which teaches the collector, the monitor and the board in one pass.

gates.title: An Uptime Monitor Watches It
gates.rule: The uptime monitor has a target for this site. Error reporting says what broke while somebody was there; the monitor is what notices when nobody is.
gates.fix: Add the target to the monitor's configuration on the Pi.

gates.title: It Appears On The Status Board
gates.rule: The site is listed on the public status page. A site being watched and a site being seen to be watched are different things, and visitors only get the second.
gates.fix: Add it to the status feed the board reads.

gates.title: A Real Error Travelled The Whole Path
gates.rule: An error thrown in a browser on the deployed site reached Discord and opened a ticket. Every step of this pipeline can be configured correctly and still not connect, and the only proof that it does is a report that made the trip.
gates.fix: Throw one deliberately on the deployed site and follow it through. A site is not onboarded until one has.
